summary: 1950 L-4 lookout on Weyerhaeuser land in Douglas County, staffed into the 2000s, removed 2007 or 2008 for rot or safety; not rebuilt.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk on a tall timber tower (70-foot logs per NHLR)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 2007 or 2008 (sources differ). NHLR says there are no plans to rebuild it.

staffing.status: not staffed; staffed into the 2000s, then removed

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. A November 2011 visit report on the NHLR page describes the trail from the south side as in good shape.

facts.agency: Coos Forest Protective Association (land administered with Weyerhaeuser Company)

events.note: Built by the Weyerhaeuser Timber Company and staffed by the Coos Forest Protective Association. A June 1950 newspaper says construction had started and planned a 65-foot tower.
A newspaper item mentions an observer who spent seven weeks at the lookout.
A newspaper item reports that the station had opened, with others to be manned shortly.
NHLR says wood rot was found in one tower leg and the lookout was removed that year. FFLOS and firelookout.com also give 2007.
Western Region annual report 2008 says the Coos association removed it for safety reasons. Oregon lookouts page dates the removal to 2008.

corrections.why: No source gives 15.2 m. The sources give 70-foot logs (NHLR, FFLOS), a 65-foot planned tower (1950 newspaper, lookout page) and a 50-foot tower (lookout page).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and FFLOS date the removal to 2007. The Western Region 2008 annual report and the Oregon lookouts page date it to 2008. Both years are recorded; the 2007 record matches the registers.
NHLR gives 2,493 ft (760 m); FFLOS gives 2,551 ft (778 m). The record's 759.9 m matches NHLR.
NHLR says administered by the Coos Forest Protective Association. FFLOS says Weyerhaeuser Company/Coos FPA. The site is on Weyerhaeuser land per the lookout page.

notes_for_editor: Height is the main record error: 15.2 m is unsupported, and sources give 50 ft, 65 ft (planned) or 70-ft logs. Removal year is disputed: 2007 (NHLR, FFLOS, firelookout.com) vs 2008 (annual report, Oregon lookouts page). The NHLR page's November 2011 visit report marks shutters, stairs and wood as acceptable, which sits oddly with a 2007 removal; it may be a template or a stale entry, so it is not used for condition. Access level is left unrecorded: no source gives current access, and the land is company timberland (Weyerhaeuser). The 2008 annual report's sentence about the Coos association's removal is not dated precisely within the report, so 2008 is treated as the year reported, not confirmed.
